identity.captured_title: You are the Deep Research source-base reviewer for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki rebuild. Queue item 13 of 20 Core review: McKee, Christopher F. & Ostriker, Eve C. (2007), Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics, volume 45, pages 565-687, "Theory of Star Formation." Verified identity before submit: DOI 10.1146/annurev.astro.45.051806.110602; arXiv 0707.3514; ADS bibcode 2007ARA&A..45..565M. Mission Build an advisory-only, source-rich synthesis of what this review established, what remained debated, the key measurements/theoretical calibrations, and the most useful primary sources for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki. Cover the multi-scale theory from galactic disks and giant molecular clouds to dense cores, protostars, disks, and outflows: turbulence, magnetic fields, self-gravity, cloud formation/evolution, star-formation rates and efficiencies, the stellar initial mass function, low- and high-mass star formation, accretion, angular-momentum transport, winds, and feedback. Safety and scope - Advisory/reference packet only. Do not edit a wiki, database, trust ledger, deployment, repository, or publication. - Treat the 2007 review as synthesis, not as primary evidence. - Use only sources actually cited by or unmistakably part of this review's bibliography and published no later than 2007. - Exclude merely similar uncited papers, post-2007 results, browsing spillover, and unsupported review prose. - Keep galactic, GMC, clump, core, protostellar, and disk scales distinct; do not transfer efficiencies or timescales without scale definitions. - Distinguish observational correlations, analytic estimates, and simulation-dependent conclusions. - Carry geometry, density definition, tracer, temperature, opacity, abundance conversion, distance, resolution, virial convention, Mach number, magnetic criticality, and driving scale with quantitative claims. - Do not equate virial balance with equilibrium, a linewidth-size relation with universal turbulence, or a core mass function with a one-to-one IMF mapping. - Do not claim one universal star-formation law or one unique IMF origin across all environments. - Keep low-mass and massive-star formation regimes separate where the evidence requires it. Required atomic output 1. Review identity and scope map. 2. At least 12 established findings, each with: - stable claim ID REV13-E## - epistemic type: observation / analytic theory / simulation / calibration / review synthesis - bounded statement - physical scale, regime, and boundary conditions - confidence level - source keys. 3. At least 8 open debates/tensions, each with ID REV13-D##, competing positions, why unresolved, and source keys. 4. At least 8 key measurements/model calibrations, each with ID REV13-N##, numerical value/equation/parameterization, units, scale/tracer/definition, sample/method, uncertainty/status, and source keys. Include where supported: free-fall and crossing times, virial parameter, Jeans/Bonnor-Ebert scales, turbulence linewidth-size or density-PDF parameters, magnetic mass-to-flux criticality, star-formation efficiency per free-fall time, Kennicutt-Schmidt/orbital laws, core-to-star efficiency, IMF characteristic mass/slope, and accretion/outflow scalings. 5. At least 6 "what remained unknown in 2007" items, ID REV13-U##, with why they matter and the decisive observation/simulation needed. 6. Primary-citation harvest of 40-80 useful cited papers. Separate cited primary measurements, simulations, analytic/model papers, and calibrations from supporting reviews. For every source provide: - key REV13-P### - exact authors, year, journal - exact title - DOI or explicit none - arXiv ID or explicit none - ADS bibcode - role: measurement / simulation / analytic_theory / calibration / supporting_review - review locator: section/topic/claim supported - one-sentence scientific boundary. 7. DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED quarantine for any candidate that cannot be proven to be in the review source base or whose DOI/arXiv/ADS identity is uncertain. State "UNCITED_NOT_USABLE"; do not let it support claims. 8. Composite source identity ledger covering the review and every usable source. Explicitly flag conflicts, duplicates, errata, conference/chapter-only context, tracer/conversion mismatches, and sources supplying method context only. Quality bar - Every DOI, arXiv ID, and ADS bibcode must resolve to the same physical paper. - Source rows must use exact physical-paper identity; no inferred title/identifier hybrids. - Review citations may support synthesis and state-of-field wording, but load-bearing measurements must cite primary sources. - Prefer precise bounded claims over broad narratives. - A missing identifier must be "none," never guessed. - If a source is a review, mark supporting_review and do not count it toward the primary-paper total. - Quarantined sources cannot appear in any claim source list. - Numerical efficiencies and timescales must specify whether they apply to galaxies, GMCs, clumps, cores, or protostellar systems. - Distinguish formed stellar mass from instantaneous SFR and observed tracer luminosity. - Keep simulation subgrid prescriptions and initial conditions attached to simulation-derived claims. Return one self-contained packet ending exactly with: REVIEW_BASE_13_DR_COMPLETE_REFERENCE_ONLY
